結果太陽一出來，它們就跟著蒸發了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合深夜靈感爆棚卻懶得記下的時刻。「說好明天記得結果全忘光」的無奈，創作者最有共鳴。
variations: 凌晨的我是天才，早上的我完全不記得天才說過什麼。
半夜想到一句超讚的話，隔天只剩下「我好像想到什麼」。

en.content:
The smartest ideas of my entire life
all show up at 3am,
and I tell myself 'I'll definitely remember this tomorrow' —
then the sun comes up and they evaporate with the dark.
en.editorNote: For nights when inspiration strikes but you're too tired to write it down. That 'promised I'd remember and forgot everything' ache hits creatives hardest.
variations: 3am me is a genius; morning me can't recall a word the genius said.
I thought of the perfect line at midnight; by breakfast all that's left is 'I had something.'

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'I'll sleep early tonight / also me at 3:17am researching ancient plumbing systems'; rewritten with a different rabbit-hole topic

zh-tw.content:
睡前的我：今晚一定要早睡。
凌晨三點十七分的我：
認真研究鐵達尼號到底能不能兩個人一起浮在門板上。
這，就是我跟床的距離。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合本來想早睡、卻掉進冷知識黑洞的夜晚。把「立志早睡」和「深夜查怪東西」的反差寫成笑話，滑手機黨秒懂。
variations: 說好早睡的我，現在正在維基百科查一種我永遠用不到的深海魚。
十一點：我要睡了。三點：那塊門板到底夠不夠兩個人？

en.content:
Me before bed: tonight I'm sleeping early for sure.
Me at 3:17am:
seriously investigating whether two people really could've fit on that Titanic door.
That, right there, is the distance between me and sleep.
en.editorNote: For nights you meant to sleep early but fell down a trivia rabbit hole. The gap between 'early night' and '3am deep dive' is pure relatable comedy for scrollers.
variations: The me who promised an early night is now reading Wikipedia about a deep-sea fish I'll never encounter.
11pm: I'm going to sleep. 3am: okay but was that door actually big enough for two?

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'I'm in a 72-hour disagreement with my bed'; rewritten as an ongoing feud where the bed refuses to negotiate

zh-tw.content:
我跟我的床，
目前正在進行一場長達三天的冷戰。
我躺得好好的，牠就是不讓我睡，
而且完全拒絕坐下來談判。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合連續失眠好幾天、身心俱疲的時刻。把失眠寫成「跟床冷戰」，比直接喊累更有畫面又不沉重。
variations: 我對床沒有意見，是床對我有意見，而且不肯講清楚。
第三天了，我跟枕頭還是談不攏，牠堅持要我清醒。

en.content:
My bed and I
are currently three days into a cold war.
I lie down perfectly still, and it just won't let me sleep —
and it flatly refuses to sit down and negotiate.
en.editorNote: For when you've been sleepless for days and you're running on fumes. Framing insomnia as a feud with your bed is more vivid, and lighter, than just saying you're exhausted.
variations: I have no problem with my bed; my bed has a problem with me and won't explain it.
Day three, and my pillow and I still can't reach terms — it insists I stay awake.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'I tried counting sheep but they started judging me / formed a union'; rewritten as the sheep going on strike

zh-tw.content:
我試著數羊。
數到第三隻，牠們就集體坐下來罷工，
說這個時間還沒睡，是我的問題，不是牠們的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合連老招都失效、只能苦笑的失眠夜。把「數羊」擬人化成會罷工的員工，荒謬又好笑。
variations: 數羊數到一半，羊回頭問我：你到底幾點要放我們下班？
羊已經睡了，我還醒著，這場面實在有點丟臉。

en.content:
I tried counting sheep.
By the third one they all sat down and went on strike,
saying that me still being awake at this hour is my problem, not theirs.
en.editorNote: For the nights even the oldest trick fails and all you can do is laugh. Turning the sheep into striking employees makes the absurdity land.
variations: Halfway through counting, one sheep turned around and asked what time I was letting them clock out.
The sheep are asleep and I'm still awake — honestly, it's a little embarrassing.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'my brain has a to-do list from 2007' and the bed being where you remember everything you forgot; rewritten around an ancient embarrassing memory surfacing

zh-tw.content:
白天想不起來的事，我一躺上床全部都想起來了。
包括國中那次講錯話，
包括十年前那封沒回的訊息，
我的腦袋，是專門在深夜營業的懷舊倉庫。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合那種一閉眼就被陳年黑歷史突襲的夜晚。把腦袋寫成「深夜營業的懷舊倉庫」，尷尬到笑出來。
variations: 睡覺時間到，我的大腦準時播放年度尷尬回顧。
十年前的糗事現在才來找我，時機真的抓得很準。

en.content:
Everything I couldn't recall all day comes flooding back the second I lie down.
The thing I said wrong in middle school.
The message I never replied to ten years ago.
My brain is a nostalgia warehouse that only opens after midnight.
en.editorNote: For the nights old embarrassing memories ambush you the moment your eyes close. Framing your brain as an after-hours nostalgia warehouse makes the cringe funny.
variations: Bedtime arrives, and my brain punctually screens its annual cringe highlight reel.
A humiliating moment from ten years ago waits until now to visit — impeccable timing.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'if overthinking burned calories I'd be a supermodel'; rewritten as a nightly workout with reps

zh-tw.content:
如果胡思亂想會消耗熱量，
我現在應該是世界冠軍。
每天凌晨躺著練三個小時，
重量全部壓在心上。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合躺著焦慮到天亮的夜晚。把「胡思亂想」寫成一種夜間重訓，苦中帶笑。
variations: 別人半夜在睡覺，我半夜在做心理有氧，一次三小時起跳。
我沒運動的習慣，除了每晚那場停不下來的腦內馬拉松。

en.content:
If overthinking burned calories,
I'd be a world champion by now.
Three hours of it every night, lying perfectly still,
all the weight pressing straight down on my chest.
en.editorNote: For the nights you lie there anxious until dawn. Reframing overthinking as a nightly workout makes the exhaustion strangely funny.
variations: Everyone else does cardio in the morning; I do it at 2am, lying down, for three hours straight.
I don't really exercise — except for the nonstop mental marathon I run every single night.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'I don't need an alarm clock, my racing thoughts wake me up just fine'; rewritten as thoughts being an alarm you can't turn off

zh-tw.content:
我不需要鬧鐘。
每天凌晨三點，我的思緒會自動響起，
而且沒有貪睡鍵，
也找不到關掉的地方。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合每晚被自己的念頭準時吵醒的人。把思緒比喻成「沒有貪睡鍵的鬧鐘」，準到讓人哭笑不得。
variations: 全世界的鬧鐘都能關，只有我腦子裡那個關不掉。
凌晨三點準時開機的不是我，是我停不下來的腦袋。

en.content:
I don't need an alarm clock.
Every night at 3am my thoughts go off on schedule —
no snooze button,
and nowhere to switch them off.
en.editorNote: For anyone woken up punctually by their own mind every night. Comparing your thoughts to an alarm with no snooze is painfully accurate.
variations: Every alarm in the world has an off switch — except the one inside my head.
The thing that boots up at 3am sharp isn't me; it's my brain that won't power down.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by tweets about the brain running worst-case scenarios at night; rewritten as a night-shift security guard doing rounds

zh-tw.content:
凌晨兩點，我的腦袋開始巡邏：
瓦斯關了嗎？門鎖了嗎？
2019 年那封信是不是漏回了？
全公司只有牠加班，而且沒領加班費。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合躺下才開始「安全檢查」的人。把腦袋寫成盡責過頭的夜班保全，荒謬又貼切。
variations: 我腦袋是全世界最認真的保全，可惜巡的是我十年前的失誤。
門鎖三次、瓦斯看兩次，最後躺回床上繼續擔心第四次。

en.content:
2am, and my brain starts its rounds:
Stove off? Door locked?
Did I ever answer that email from 2019?
It's the only employee here working overtime, unpaid.
en.editorNote: For people whose safety inspection only begins once they lie down. Casting your brain as an over-diligent night guard makes the absurdity land.
variations: My brain is the most dedicated security guard alive — it just patrols my old mistakes.
Checked the lock three times, the stove twice, then lay back down to worry about a fourth.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'the body is tired, the thoughts are auditioning for a talent show'; rewritten as a late-night talent contest with the body as unwilling judge

zh-tw.content:
我的身體已經累到快關機，
我的思緒卻在辦一場才藝比賽。
一號選手：明天的簡報。
二號選手：高中那件丟臉的事。
而我是那個不能離席的評審。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合形容「人很累但腦很吵」的夜晚。用選秀節目的形式排列煩惱，讀起來有畫面又好笑。
variations: 身體想睡，腦袋想紅，兩邊每晚都談不攏。
我不是失眠，我只是被自己的煩惱綁去當評審。

en.content:
My body is running on fumes.
My thoughts are holding auditions.
Contestant one: tomorrow's presentation.
Contestant two: that thing I said in high school.
And I'm the judge who isn't allowed to leave.
en.editorNote: Perfect for the classic tired-body-loud-brain night. Framing your worries as a talent show gives the exhaustion a punchline.
variations: My body wants sleep, my brain wants stage time — negotiations fail nightly.
It's not insomnia, I've just been drafted as a judge by my own anxieties.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'I can't sleep because I'm stressed, I'm stressed because I can't sleep — the only winner is coffee companies'; rewritten with a local coffee shop owner

zh-tw.content:
我睡不著，是因為壓力大；
我壓力大，是因為睡不著。
這個圈我繞了三年，
目前唯一的受益者，是巷口那家咖啡店老闆。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合分享給每天靠咖啡續命的同事。用「受益者是咖啡店老闆」收尾，苦笑感剛剛好。
variations: 失眠是一個圓，起點是壓力，終點也是壓力，中間是三杯美式。
我這輩子最忠誠的關係，是我跟巷口那家咖啡店。

en.content:
I can't sleep because I'm stressed.
I'm stressed because I can't sleep.
Three years in this loop,
and the only one profiting is the coffee shop on my corner.
en.editorNote: Send this to the coworker running on caffeine. Ending on the coffee shop owner turns the vicious cycle into a wry joke.
variations: Insomnia is a circle: stress at the start, stress at the end, three americanos in between.
The most loyal relationship of my life is with the cafe downstairs.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'you do the tea, the no phone, the pretend meditation, then midnight shows up with a to-do list in a trench coat'; rewritten with local details

zh-tw.content:
我泡了洋甘菊、關了手機、
認真冥想了二十分鐘——
其中十九分鐘在想鹹酥雞。
然後午夜穿著風衣出現，
手上拿著我明天的待辦清單。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合所有睡前儀式做好做滿、還是失敗的人。結尾把午夜擬人成談判對手，畫面很有戲。
variations: 睡前儀式我一項都沒少，少的只有睡意。
冥想到最後我什麼都放下了，除了明天要交的東西。

en.content:
Chamomile tea: done. Phone away: done.
Twenty minutes of serious meditation —
nineteen of them spent thinking about fried chicken.
Then midnight strolls in wearing a trench coat,
holding tomorrow's to-do list.
en.editorNote: For everyone who nails the whole bedtime routine and still loses. Personifying midnight as a trench-coated visitor gives it a cinematic kick.
variations: I did every step of the wind-down routine. The only thing missing was sleep.
By the end of the meditation I had let go of everything except tomorrow's deadline.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the hypnic jerk phenomenon (the falling sensation that jolts you awake right at sleep onset); rewritten as the body sabotaging its own landing

zh-tw.content:
好不容易快睡著了，
身體突然覺得我在往下墜，
猛力抽了一下，把我救回清醒。
謝謝喔，我根本沒事，
是你自己嚇自己，順便嚇醒我。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合形容那種「將睡未睡卻被自己踢醒」的崩潰。把抽動寫成身體自導自演的假救援，荒謬感很到位。
variations: 我的身體是全世界最盡責的救生員，專門把沒溺水的我從睡眠裡撈起來。
睡到一半覺得踩空，抽一下醒來——原來危險的只有我想睡這件事。

en.content:
I was finally drifting off,
when my body decided I was falling,
and yanked me back to fully awake.
Thanks, but I was fine —
you scared yourself, and dragged me down with you.
en.editorNote: For that specific betrayal of jerking awake at the exact edge of sleep. Framing the twitch as a fake rescue nobody asked for lands the absurdity.
variations: My body is the most dedicated lifeguard alive — it keeps pulling me out of a sleep I wasn't drowning in.
Half asleep, I feel myself miss a step, jolt awake — turns out the only danger was me getting sleepy.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the universal 'finally got comfortable, now I need to pee' bedtime joke; rewritten with the perfect-position setup and bladder punchline

zh-tw.content:
翻了半小時，終於喬到完美的姿勢。
棉被溫度剛好，枕頭角度剛好，
連呼吸都剛好。
就在這一秒，我的膀胱舉手發言：
欸，我想上廁所。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合分享給每天為了睡姿奮鬥的人。把膀胱擬人成最不會看場合的舉手發言者，笑點又氣又真實。
variations: 宇宙給了我完美睡姿，然後派膀胱來收回這份禮物。
好不容易全身都對位了，唯一不配合的器官選在這時候上線。

en.content:
Half an hour of shuffling, and I finally hit the perfect position.
Blanket at the right warmth, pillow at the right angle,
even my breathing lined up.
Right at that second, my bladder raises its hand:
um, I need to pee.
en.editorNote: Send this to anyone who fights for the ideal sleeping position nightly. Casting the bladder as the worst-timed hand-raiser makes the betrayal funny.
variations: The universe handed me the perfect sleeping position, then sent my bladder to take it back.
Everything finally aligned, and the one organ that refused to cooperate picked that moment to log on.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the dread of still being awake when the sky lightens; rewritten with dawn birdsong as the official signal you lost the night

zh-tw.content:
凌晨還在跟睡意拔河，
窗外的鳥開始唱歌了。
那不是浪漫，那是裁判吹哨：
本場比賽結束，
睡眠零分，你正式輸掉今晚。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合形容熬到天快亮的絕望。把鳥鳴寫成宣判失敗的哨聲，苦中帶笑，很多夜貓子會秒懂。
variations: 當第一隻鳥開口，我就知道，今晚這場我認輸了。
別人聽鳥叫是清晨，我聽鳥叫是敗戰通知。

en.content:
Still tugging at sleep in the small hours,
when the birds outside start to sing.
That's not romance, that's the referee's whistle:
game over,
sleep zero, and you officially lost tonight.
en.editorNote: For the despair of pushing right up to sunrise. Recasting the dawn chorus as a whistle that calls the match makes the defeat wryly funny — every night owl gets it.
variations: The moment the first bird opens its beak, I know I've surrendered tonight.
For everyone else, birdsong means morning. For me, it's a notice that I lost.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'work can wait, my dreams can't' and stress-dream jokes; rewritten as the rare night you sleep but dream about work, so even sleep bills overtime

zh-tw.content:
好不容易有一晚真的睡著了。
結果我夢到自己在加班，
開了三場會，還被主管釘。
醒來比沒睡還累——
原來我連夢裡都在打卡，而且沒有加班費。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合所有「睡了也沒回血」的上班族。把夢境寫成無薪加班，把失眠的疲憊延伸到睡著也逃不掉，共鳴很強。
variations: 難得睡著，卻夢到明天要交的東西，等於免費幫公司值了一班夜。
我的夢不放假，主管在夢裡也照樣找得到我。

en.content:
For once, I actually fell asleep.
Then I dreamed I was working overtime,
sat through three meetings, got chewed out by my boss.
Woke up more tired than if I'd stayed up —
turns out I clock in even in my dreams, still unpaid.
en.editorNote: For every worker whose sleep never refills the tank. Framing the stress dream as unpaid overtime extends the exhaustion into sleep itself — painfully relatable.
variations: The rare night I sleep, I dream about tomorrow's deadline — basically a free night shift for the company.
My dreams don't take days off, and my boss can find me in them too.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by subverting the 'sleep like a baby' idiom; rewritten to point out babies actually wake every couple of hours

zh-tw.content:
他們安慰我，希望我今晚睡得像嬰兒一樣。
謝謝，我還真的做到了：
每兩小時醒一次，
醒來一臉茫然，
而且很想哭。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合吐槽「睡得像嬰兒」這個安慰有多不準。把成語照字面拆開反諷，短短幾句就翻轉整個祝福，很好笑。
variations: 叫我睡得像嬰兒？我已經很敬業了，每兩小時準時哭醒一次。
睡得像嬰兒不是誇獎，是每晚醒五次、還搞不清楚自己在哪。

en.content:
They told me they hoped I'd sleep like a baby tonight.
Thanks — I actually pulled it off:
waking up every two hours,
blinking in confusion,
and kind of wanting to cry.
en.editorNote: For roasting how useless the 'sleep like a baby' line really is. Taking the idiom literally flips the whole blessing into a joke in a few short lines.
variations: Sleep like a baby? I'm nailing it — waking up crying right on schedule every two hours.
Sleeping like a baby isn't a compliment: it's waking five times a night with no idea where you are.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the classic 'partner falls asleep the second their head hits the pillow while I lie awake' contrast; rewritten with the sleeper snoring and the awake one negotiating with the universe

zh-tw.content:
我旁邊的人，頭一碰枕頭三秒就睡著，還打起呼。
而我睜著眼睛，開始認真思考：
我們的關係、宇宙的盡頭、
還有冰箱裡那盒放到過期的優格。
同一張床，兩個世界。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合枕邊人秒睡、自己卻清醒到天亮的夜晚。用「同一張床，兩個世界」收尾，情侶或室友都超有感。
variations: 他打呼的頻率，剛好變成我今晚的白噪音，而且還沒有暫停鍵。
看著身邊的人三秒入睡，我第一次體會到什麼叫望塵莫及。

en.content:
The person next to me was out cold three seconds after hitting the pillow, snoring already.
Meanwhile I'm lying here wide awake, seriously pondering:
our relationship, the edge of the universe,
and that carton of yogurt I let expire in the fridge.
Same bed, two different worlds.
en.editorNote: For the night your partner passes out instantly while you're up till dawn. The 'same bed, two worlds' closer lands hard for couples and roommates alike.
variations: His snoring is basically my white noise tonight, except there's no pause button.
Watching someone fall asleep in three seconds, I finally understand what 'out of my league' means.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the 'one leg out of the blanket as temperature control' meme; rewritten as manually operating yourself like an air conditioner all night

zh-tw.content:
我整晚都在調節體溫。
棉被全蓋太熱，全掀太冷，
所以我伸出一隻腳當散熱器，
翻面找還沒被睡熱的那側，
蓋一半、掀一半、再翻一次。
凌晨四點，我不是在睡覺，
我是在手動當一台恆溫空調。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合為了棉被溫度翻來覆去一整晚的人。把「一隻腳伸出被子」寫成散熱器，荒謬又精準，畫面感十足。
variations: 我的一隻腳負責散熱，另一隻負責保暖，它們今晚都沒睡。
枕頭睡熱了就翻面找涼的那側，我這輩子最勤勞的時刻都花在半夜的床上。

en.content:
I spent the whole night regulating my body temperature.
Blanket fully on: too hot. Fully off: too cold.
So I stick one leg out as a radiator,
flip to the side I haven't warmed up yet,
half covered, half uncovered, flip again.
By 4am I'm not sleeping,
I'm manually operating myself like an air conditioner.
en.editorNote: For anyone who tosses all night fighting the blanket temperature. Framing the one-leg-out move as a radiator is absurd and painfully accurate.
variations: One leg handles cooling, the other handles heating, and neither of them slept tonight.
The pillow gets warm, so I flip it to the cool side — the hardest I work all day is in bed at 3am.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by sleep-app / white-noise culture; rewritten as the rain-sound track backfiring because you start analyzing the audio loop instead of sleeping

zh-tw.content:
為了助眠，我打開了「雨聲」。
聽著聽著，我的腦袋開始運轉：
這雨到底下多久了？會不會淹水？
欸這段音檔，是不是每三分鐘就 loop 一次？
剛剛那聲雷，上一輪好像也在同個位置。
助眠 App 成功了——它讓我更清醒了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合吐槽助眠音效反而讓人更醒的夜晚。腦袋開始分析音檔迴圈的細節，把「越努力助眠越睡不著」寫得很好笑。
variations: 我開了海浪聲助眠，結果整晚在數這波浪到底幾秒打一次。
白噪音沒把我催眠，反而讓我升職成了它的音檔品管人員。

en.content:
To help me sleep, I put on 'rain sounds.'
A few minutes in, my brain fires up:
How long has this rain been falling? Is it going to flood?
Wait — does this track loop every three minutes?
That thunderclap was in the exact same spot last time around.
The sleep app worked — it made me even more awake.
en.editorNote: For roasting how sleep sounds keep you up instead. Your brain dissecting the audio loop nails the 'the harder I try to sleep, the more awake I get' bit.
variations: Put on ocean waves to fall asleep, spent the whole night counting how many seconds between each wave.
The white noise didn't hypnotize me — it just promoted me to its unpaid quality-control inspector.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the 'revenge bedtime procrastination' concept; rewritten as refusing to sleep because the night is the only time that belongs to you

zh-tw.content:
我明明累到不行，卻死撐著不睡。
不是睡不著，是不甘心——
這一天從頭到尾都是別人的，
只有現在這幾個小時，終於輪到我。
一閉眼，明天就開始了，
所以我選擇，多偷一點今天。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合「報復性熬夜」的人。點出不是失眠，是捨不得把僅剩的自由時間交出去，很多上班族一看就中。
variations: 我不是不想睡，是不想這麼快就把今天還給世界。
白天都在為別人活，凌晨兩點這段，是我唯一的個人時間。

en.content:
I'm exhausted, but I refuse to sleep.
It's not that I can't — it's that I won't.
The whole day belonged to everyone else,
and these few hours are finally mine.
The second I close my eyes, tomorrow starts,
so I keep stealing a little more of today.
en.editorNote: For the revenge-bedtime-procrastination crowd. It names the real reason you stay up — not insomnia, just refusing to hand over the only free time you have.
variations: I don't hate sleep. I just don't want to give today back this soon.
I spent all day living for other people. 2am is the only shift that's mine.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 3am-brain / health-anxiety memes; rewritten as googling a tiny symptom and escalating to planning your own funeral

zh-tw.content:
凌晨三點，我搜尋了一個小症狀。
第一頁：可能是太累。
第三頁：可能有點缺水。
第七頁：建議立刻就醫。
十分鐘後，我已經在腦中，
把自己的告別式流程排好了，
連背景音樂都選好了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合半夜手滑查症狀、越查越嚴重的人。把「小症狀→安排後事」的災難化過程寫得很有畫面，健康焦慮的人秒懂。
variations: 白天覺得沒事的小毛病，凌晨一查，直接升級成絕症。
搜尋引擎凌晨三點的建議只有一種：你快沒救了，請盡快就醫。

en.content:
3am. I googled one small symptom.
Page one: probably just tired.
Page three: possibly a little dehydrated.
Page seven: seek medical attention immediately.
Ten minutes later I've mentally planned
my entire funeral, playlist included.
en.editorNote: For anyone who fat-fingers a symptom search at night and spirals. The 'minor symptom to funeral arrangements' escalation nails 3am health anxiety.
variations: A tiny ache I ignored all day becomes terminal the second I search it at 3am.
Every symptom search at 3am ends the same way: 'see a doctor now, it may be too late.'

items.sourceNote: Inspired by insomnia memes about night noise; rewritten as sudden hypersensitivity to the fridge hum, dripping faucet and ticking clock

zh-tw.content:
白天完全聽不到的冰箱嗡嗡聲，
到了凌晨三點，變成整個房間最大聲的東西。
接著我聽見水龍頭在滴、時鐘在走、
樓上有人翻身。
一旦聽見，就再也關不掉，
我的耳朵，深夜自動升級成監視器。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合半夜對細微聲音特別敏感的人。冰箱、滴水、秒針——白天無感，凌晨全部放大。把「一旦聽見就關不掉」寫得很精準。
variations: 凌晨三點，我家最吵的三個住戶是：冰箱、水龍頭、跟我的耳朵。
白天像個聾子，凌晨三點突然練成順風耳，連隔壁的時鐘都聽得一清二楚。

en.content:
The fridge hum I can't hear all day
becomes the loudest thing in the room at 3am.
Then I catch the faucet dripping, the clock ticking,
someone upstairs rolling over.
Once I hear it, I can't un-hear it —
my ears quietly upgrade to surveillance mode at night.
en.editorNote: For anyone whose hearing goes supersonic at 3am. The fridge, the drip, the second hand — inaudible by day, deafening at night, and impossible to tune back out.
variations: At 3am the three loudest tenants in my apartment are the fridge, the faucet, and my own ears.
Deaf all day, then at 3am I can suddenly hear the neighbor's clock ticking through the wall.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by insomnia humor; rewritten as literal envy of a pet that sleeps sixteen hours a day while you can't scrape together five

zh-tw.content:
我家的貓一天睡十六小時，
醒來還打了個哈欠，一臉沒睡飽。
我一天連五小時都湊不齊，
白天卻得裝作精神很好。
我們住同一個屋簷下，
命運怎麼可以差這麼多。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合養寵物又長期睡不飽的人。看著整天狂睡的貓狗，對比自己搶不到幾小時睡眠，又好氣又好笑。
variations: 我家的貓把我這輩子欠的睡眠，全部替我睡回來了。
同一個屋簷下，牠負責睡，我負責醒，分工明確。

en.content:
My cat sleeps sixteen hours a day,
wakes up, yawns, and still looks underslept.
I can't even scrape together five,
yet I have to act functional by daylight.
We live under the same roof —
how are our fates this different?
en.editorNote: For pet owners running on empty. Watching your cat or dog sleep all day while you can't steal five hours is equal parts funny and unfair.
variations: My cat is out here sleeping off the entire sleep debt I've racked up for both of us.
Same roof, clear division of labor: he handles the sleeping, I handle the being awake.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by summer heat-wave humor about the single mosquito ruining a night's sleep; rewritten as an all-night stalemate that you 'win' by suffocating under the blanket

zh-tw.content:
凌晨兩點，房間裡有一隻蚊子。
開燈，牠消失；關燈，牠就貼著我耳朵開嗓。
我揮了三十次空氣，開了七次燈，
最後整個人縮進棉被，只露一個鼻孔。
熱到快融化，但至少我沒被叮到。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合夏天被一隻蚊子搞到徹底清醒的夜晚。「開燈就消失、關燈就出現」是全民共同記憶，最後躲進棉被的慘勝很有畫面。
variations: 今晚唯一跟我有互動的生物，是一隻蚊子。
睡不著我可以接受，睡不著還被叮，我沒辦法接受。

en.content:
2am, and there is exactly one mosquito in this room.
Lights on: gone. Lights off: right back at my ear, warming up.
I've swung at empty air thirty times and flipped the switch seven,
so now I'm burrowed under the blanket with one nostril out.
Melting alive, but at least I didn't get bitten.
en.editorNote: For the summer night one mosquito wakes you up completely. The lights-on-it-vanishes bit is universal, and surrendering under the blanket makes for a great miserable victory.
variations: The only living thing I interacted with tonight was a mosquito.
I can accept not sleeping. I cannot accept not sleeping AND getting bitten.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by summer reporting on AC temperature and sleep; rewritten as an absurd infinite loop of AC on/off plus blanket on/off, with the electric bill as the punchline

zh-tw.content:
夏天的睡覺流程是這樣的：
開冷氣，冷到要蓋棉被；
蓋了棉被，熱到要掀開；
掀開棉被，冷到要關冷氣；
關了冷氣，熱到要再開一次。
我花錢把房間弄冷，再蓋棉被把自己弄暖，
這一整套流程裡，只有電費是清醒的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合每晚跟冷氣遙控器拉鋸的人。用無限迴圈的寫法堆疊荒謬，最後用「只有電費是清醒的」收尾，夏天發限動超有共鳴。
variations: 遙控器在我手上按了一整晚，唯一睡著的是我的判斷力。
二十六度太熱、二十五度太冷，我的人生就卡在這一度中間。

en.content:
My summer bedtime routine goes like this:
Turn the AC on — now it's cold, so I need a blanket.
Pull the blanket up — now it's hot, so I kick it off.
Kick it off — now it's cold, so I kill the AC.
Kill the AC — now it's hot, so I turn it back on.
I pay money to make the room cold, then use a blanket to make myself warm.
The only thing fully awake in this loop is my electric bill.
en.editorNote: For anyone locked in nightly combat with the AC remote. The infinite loop stacks the absurdity, and the electric bill closer makes it a perfect summer caption.
variations: I pressed that remote all night. The only thing that fell asleep was my judgment.
78 is too warm, 77 is too cold, and my whole life is stuck in that one degree.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by summer memes about surviving on a single oscillating fan; rewritten as a hot-and-cold romance with the fan, playing on the double meaning of 忽冷忽熱

zh-tw.content:
電風扇轉走的時候，我在等。
轉回來的那三秒，是我今晚唯一的快樂。
然後它又走了。
凌晨三點，我躺在床上，
跟一台忽冷忽熱的機器，談了一整晚的戀愛。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合家裡只有電風扇、沒冷氣的夏夜。「忽冷忽熱」一語雙關，把等風的三秒寫成感情戲，苦中作樂剛剛好。
variations: 我這輩子最專心等待的東西，是電風扇轉回來的那三秒。
與其說我在睡覺，不如說我整晚都在排隊等風。

en.content:
When the fan turns away, I wait.
Those three seconds when it swings back are the only joy I get all night.
Then it leaves again.
3am, flat on my back, having a full hot-and-cold romance
with a machine that keeps turning its head away from me.
en.editorNote: For hot nights with a fan and no AC. Framing the three-second wait as a romance with something that literally blows hot and cold turns misery into a decent joke.
variations: The thing I've waited for most intently in my life is the fan swinging back around.
I'm not sleeping so much as standing in line for wind all night.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by heat-wave sleep coverage mentioning cool showers; rewritten as the shower's effect expiring on a minute-by-minute countdown, with a video-game save-point punchline

zh-tw.content:
睡前沖了個冷水澡，全身涼快，信心滿滿。
躺上床第三分鐘，額頭開始冒汗；
第八分鐘，背黏在床單上；
第十五分鐘，我已經完整回到洗澡前的狀態。
夏天的睡眠，是一款沒有存檔點的遊戲。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合夏天洗完澡躺下沒多久又流汗的人。用分鐘倒數推進，越讀越絕望；結尾的「沒有存檔點」把整晚重來的感覺講得很精準。
variations: 冷水澡的有效期限是十五分鐘，比我的意志力還短。
我不是睡不著，我只是每晚都得重洗一次澡，才能重新開始。

en.content:
Took a cool shower before bed. Felt amazing. Full of confidence.
Minute three in bed: forehead sweating.
Minute eight: back glued to the sheet.
Minute fifteen: I am exactly where I was before the shower.
Summer sleep is a game with no save points.
en.editorNote: For anyone who showers, lies down, and is sweating again within minutes. The minute-by-minute countdown builds the despair, and 'no save points' nails having to start the whole night over.
variations: A cold shower lasts fifteen minutes, which is still longer than my willpower.
It's not that I can't sleep, it's that I have to re-shower every night just to restart the attempt.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by coverage of hot nights costing people sleep worldwide; rewritten as a gentle companionship piece about everyone else who is also awake in the same heat

zh-tw.content:
熱到睡不著的夏夜，會覺得全世界只剩你醒著。
其實不是。
同一片悶熱裡，有人站在陽台等一陣風，
有人走進便利商店買第二罐冰的，
有人跟你一樣，剛翻完第八次身。
這個夏天的凌晨三點，比你以為的還要熱鬧。
睡不著沒關係，天會涼，這個夜也會過去。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給最近被高溫熬到崩潰的朋友。不給建議、不叫人早點睡，只是把「你不是唯一醒著的那個」輕輕放在他手上。
variations: 夏天的夜晚很長，但你不是一個人在撐。
睡不著的時候至少可以想想：這座城市裡，還有很多盞燈跟你一起亮著。

en.content:
On a night too hot to sleep, it feels like you're the only one awake in the world.
You're not.
Somewhere in the same heat, someone's on a balcony waiting for a breeze,
someone's in a convenience store buying a second cold drink,
someone just rolled over for the eighth time, exactly like you.
3am this summer is busier than you think.
It's okay not to sleep. The heat will break, and so will this night.
en.editorNote: Send this to the friend the heat wave has been wrecking. No advice, no 'just go to bed earlier' — just a quiet reminder that they aren't the only one still up.
variations: Summer nights run long, but you're not getting through this one alone.
When you can't sleep, remember there are plenty of other lights still on across this city.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the well-documented 'can fall asleep on the couch but not in bed' phenomenon; rewritten as a bewildered self-observation

zh-tw.content:
在沙發上，我十分鐘就昏過去。
一移到床上躺好，眼睛立刻亮得像剛充飽電。
我懷疑我的身體，是故意的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合貼在你又在客廳睡著、被叫醒後死活躺回床上卻清醒到天亮的那種夜晚。誰家都有這一位背骨的身體。
variations: 沙發：秒睡。床：開機。這中間到底發生了什麼事？
我不是失眠，我只是床認證系統一直失敗。

en.content:
On the couch, I'm out cold in ten minutes.
The second I move to the bed and lie down properly, my eyes light up like they just hit a full charge.
I'm starting to think my body does this on purpose.
en.editorNote: For the night you knocked out on the sofa, got herded to bed, and then stayed wide awake until sunrise. Everyone's body has this one traitor in it.
variations: Couch: instant sleep. Bed: system boot-up. What happens in those ten steps?
I don't have insomnia. My bed's authentication just keeps failing.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the running joke about melatonin gummies doing nothing; rewritten with a customer-review framing

zh-tw.content:
吃了褪黑激素軟糖，等它發揮神效。
一小時後：清醒。
兩小時後：非常清醒。
三小時後：我開始煩惱這罐是不是快過期了。
給一顆星，唯一的作用是變成宵夜。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合那種買了各種助眠小物、結果全部無效還越吃越餓的夜晚。把它當成假掰的商品評論來寫，特別好笑。
variations: 助眠軟糖的功效：讓我多一件睡不著時可以怪罪的東西。
說明書寫30分鐘見效，我第30分鐘正在思考人生。

en.content:
Took a melatonin gummy, waited for the magic.
One hour later: awake.
Two hours later: very awake.
Three hours later: I'm now worried the bottle's about to expire.
One star. Its only real function was being a midnight snack.
en.editorNote: For the night you bought every sleep aid on the shelf and they all did nothing except make you hungrier. Writing it as a fake product review is what sells it.
variations: What the sleep gummies actually do: give me one more thing to blame when I can't sleep.
Label says works in 30 minutes. At minute 30 I was reevaluating my entire life.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the classic intrusive-thought meme where the brain reminds you that you breathe and blink manually; rewritten as a nightly notification

zh-tw.content:
正要睡著，大腦突然彈出通知：
提醒你，你現在是手動呼吸。
還有，你剛剛注意到自己在眨眼了，接下來每一次都要自己數。
謝謝，這下我今晚不用睡了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合那種本來快睡著、卻被自己腦袋硬生生叫醒的瞬間。看到的人會忍不住開始注意自己的呼吸——傳給朋友一起清醒。
variations: 大腦：欸，你有發現你的舌頭現在不知道該放哪嗎？
本來要睡了，結果開始手動呼吸，這局我輸了。

en.content:
Right as I'm drifting off, my brain sends a notification:
reminder, you are now breathing manually.
Also, you just noticed yourself blinking, so from here on you'll be counting every one.
Thanks. Guess I'm not sleeping tonight.
en.editorNote: For the exact moment your own brain yanks you back awake from the edge of sleep. Anyone who reads it will immediately notice their own breathing — send it and suffer together.
variations: Brain: hey, have you noticed your tongue doesn't know where to sit right now?
Was about to fall asleep, then started breathing manually. I lose this round.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the '3am is when you have your best ideas' tweet theme; rewritten around the idea evaporating by morning

zh-tw.content:
凌晨三點，我想出了一個能改變人生的絕妙點子。
我告訴自己，這麼厲害一定記得住，不用寫下來。
早上醒來，我只記得它「很厲害」，內容完全空白。
我的一生功業，就這樣被睡意吃掉了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合那種半夜靈感爆棚、隔天卻一片空白的懊悔時刻。提醒大家：再睏也要把點子打進手機備忘錄。
variations: 凌晨的我是天才，早上的我是他的無能助理，什麼都沒抄到。
那個能讓我財富自由的點子，昨晚被我英勇地忘記了。

en.content:
At 3am I came up with a brilliant, life-changing idea.
I told myself something this good, I'd obviously remember — no need to write it down.
Woke up and all I've got is that it was 'brilliant.' The actual content: blank.
My life's masterpiece, eaten alive by drowsiness.
en.editorNote: For the regret of a midnight stroke of genius that's gone by breakfast. Public service reminder: no matter how sleepy, type the idea into your phone.
variations: 3am me is a genius. Morning me is his useless assistant who took zero notes.
The idea that would've made me financially free? I heroically forgot it last night.

items.sourceNote: Original gentle piece written to balance the joke items; reframes a sleepless night as permission to stop trying so hard

zh-tw.content:
睡不著的時候，你最常做的事，是逼自己趕快睡。
但睡眠不是考試，越用力越拿不到分數。
今晚就先別逼了。
把「一定要睡著」這件事，從待辦清單上劃掉，
剩下的，交給時間就好。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那種一躺下就開始跟自己較勁、越想睡越清醒的朋友。核心是把「入睡」從任務降級成順其自然，讓對方鬆一口氣。
variations: 今晚的任務不是睡著，是別再責怪睡不著的自己。
放過自己一晚，睡眠通常會在你不追的時候自己回來。

en.content:
When you can't sleep, the thing you do most is force yourself to sleep faster.
But sleep isn't a test — the harder you push, the lower the score.
So don't push tonight.
Cross 'must fall asleep' off the to-do list,
and leave the rest to time.
en.editorNote: Send this to the friend who lies down and immediately starts wrestling with themselves, getting more awake the harder they try. The point is to demote 'falling asleep' from a task to something that just happens — and let them exhale.
variations: Tonight's job isn't to fall asleep. It's to stop blaming yourself for being awake.
Let yourself off the hook for one night. Sleep usually comes back when you stop chasing it.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by JoJo Jensen 'without enough sleep we all become tall two-year-olds'; rewritten with concrete symptoms and a self-aware tone

zh-tw.content:
睡不夠的我，本質上就是一個長太高的兩歲小孩。
會無緣無故想哭，會為了超小的事發脾氣，
還需要有人提醒我，該去躺著了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 轉給那種一睡不飽就情緒失控、看個廣告都能掉眼淚的朋友，他會邊笑邊點頭承認。
variations: 別惹睡不飽的我，我現在的情緒管理等級，跟幼兒園小班差不多。

en.content:
Running on no sleep, I'm basically a two-year-old who happens to be tall.
I cry for no reason, throw a fit over the tiniest things,
and I still need someone to remind me it's time to lie down.
en.editorNote: Send this to the friend who becomes emotionally unhinged the second they're underslept — the one who tears up at a commercial. They'll laugh and nod.
variations: Don't test me on no sleep. My emotional regulation is currently at preschool level.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'tired since 2017, running on vibes and iced coffee' tweet format; rewritten around caffeine plus spite as fuel

zh-tw.content:
問我累不累？
我不是今天才累，我是從某一年開始，就再也沒真正睡飽過。
現在完全靠咖啡因，和一股不服氣，硬撐著。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合那種長期慢性疲勞、已經忘記「精神好」是什麼感覺的人。「哪一年開始的」講不出來，反而最有共鳴。
variations: 我的能量來源有兩個：一杯冰美式，還有『我就不信我今天撐不過去』。

en.content:
Ask me if I'm tired?
I'm not tired from today. I haven't slept properly since some year I've honestly lost track of.
At this point I'm running purely on caffeine and pure spite.
en.editorNote: For the chronically exhausted — the ones who no longer remember what 'well-rested' feels like. Not being able to name the year is the part that lands.
variations: My two energy sources: an iced americano, and refusing to admit I can't make it through the day.

items.sourceNote: Original take on the 'waking at the same time every night' experience; framed as a body clock that's punctual only for the wrong thing

zh-tw.content:
我的生理時鐘什麼都記不住。
該起床的鬧鐘按掉三次，該吃飯的時間全忘光，
唯獨每天凌晨三點四十七分，準時把我叫醒——分秒不差。
zh-tw.editorNote: 獻給那種每晚都在同一個詭異時間自動睜眼的人。身體其他事全遲到，只有這件事超級準時。
variations: 我的身體對所有事都遲到，只有『半夜自動清醒』這項服務，全年無休、從不誤點。

en.content:
My body clock can't remember a single thing.
It snoozes the morning alarm three times, forgets every mealtime,
yet every single night at 3:47am, it wakes me up right on the dot. Not a minute off.
en.editorNote: For anyone who snaps awake at the same strange hour every night. Their body is late for everything else — this is the one thing it nails perfectly.
variations: My body is late for everything. Except the nightly wake-up call — that service runs 365 days a year, never delayed.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by weekend catch-up sleep humor; reframed as sleep debt with compound interest, a fresh loan-shark angle

zh-tw.content:
睡眠負債這種東西，比信用卡還狠。
週末想一次還清，它說：不好意思，這還沒加利息。
我這輩子大概是還不完了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 轉給那種週末補眠到下午、起床還是覺得沒回本的朋友。睡眠債只會利滾利，越補越覺得虧。
variations: 別人存錢生利息，我欠睡眠生利息，而且是複利。

en.content:
Sleep debt is more ruthless than any credit card.
Try to pay it all back on the weekend, and it goes: sorry, that's before interest.
I don't think I'll ever clear this balance.
en.editorNote: For the friend who sleeps till 3pm on Saturday and still wakes up in the red. Sleep debt only compounds — the more you catch up, the more you owe.
variations: Other people earn compound interest on their savings. I owe compound interest on sleep.

items.sourceNote: Original personification of insomnia as a freeloading live-in roommate; distinct from existing Wi-Fi-roommate and ceiling-relationship items

zh-tw.content:
失眠這位室友，是自己搬進來的，從沒問過我。
不付房租、不做家事，每天準時霸佔整個晚上，
還把我的睡眠當公共財，想用就用。
我甚至趕不走牠，因為合約上簽名的，好像是我自己。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那種「失眠已經變成日常」的朋友。把失眠擬人化成賴著不走的室友，荒謬又貼切，苦中作樂剛剛好。
variations: 我沒有養寵物，但我有一位叫失眠的室友，牠二十四小時都在家。

en.content:
Insomnia moved in without asking. Never signed a lease, never paid a cent.
Doesn't do the dishes, doesn't cover rent — just claims the entire night, every night,
and treats my sleep like it's communal property.
I can't even evict it, because the name on the contract appears to be mine.
en.editorNote: For the friend whose insomnia has become a permanent housemate. Framing it as a freeloader who won't leave makes the misery weirdly funny.
variations: I don't have a pet, but I do have a roommate named Insomnia. It's home twenty-four hours a day.

items.sourceNote: Original take on the 3am overthinking spiral reframed as an abandoned home renovation; renovation/furniture angle absent from existing items

zh-tw.content:
凌晨三點，我的腦袋決定幫我的人生重新裝潢。
先把整套計畫敲掉，家具搬來搬去，
連童年都翻出來重新粉刷了一遍。
結果天一亮，工程無限期停工，
留下一個爛尾的我，跟滿地想不起來的靈感。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合半夜突然開始「重新規劃整個人生」、天亮卻什麼都沒留下的時候。把深夜的胡思亂想寫成一場爛尾工程，畫面感十足。
variations: 我半夜把人生重新設計了三次，早上起來連原本的版本都忘了。

en.content:
At 3am my brain decides to renovate my entire life.
It tears down the whole plan, drags the furniture around,
even digs up my childhood for a fresh coat of paint.
Then the sun comes up, the project is suspended indefinitely,
and all that's left is a half-gutted me and a floor full of ideas I can't remember.
en.editorNote: For when you spend the small hours redesigning your whole life and wake up with nothing to show for it. Framing the midnight spiral as an abandoned renovation makes it land.
variations: I redesigned my life three times last night. By morning I couldn't even remember the original.

items.sourceNote: Original 'just resting my eyes' denial cope; the 閉目養神 framing does not appear in existing items

zh-tw.content:
我沒有睡不著，我只是在「閉目養神」。
非常認真地養，一養就是六個小時，
中間還翻了四次身、查了兩次時間、想了半段人生。
你看，我這麼努力休息，怎麼能說我失眠呢？
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合嘴硬不肯承認自己失眠的人。用「閉目養神」當遮羞布，越解釋越好笑，傳群組會有人接「我也在養，養到天亮」。
variations: 我不是失眠，我只是躺著閉眼睛，順便清醒了一整晚而已。

en.content:
I'm not failing to sleep. I'm just "resting my eyes."
Very diligently — six hours of it,
with four position changes, two clock checks, and half a life story in between.
See? I'm trying this hard to rest. How could you possibly call that insomnia?
en.editorNote: For the person too stubborn to admit they can't sleep. 'Just resting my eyes' as a cover story only gets funnier the more you defend it.
variations: I don't have insomnia. I just lie down with my eyes closed and stay fully conscious till dawn.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by 'I don't do drugs, I do 3am thoughts repeatedly'; rewritten as an addiction with an escalating dose

zh-tw.content:
我不碰菸酒，也不熬夜追劇。
我唯一戒不掉的癮，是凌晨三點的胡思亂想。
明知道對身體不好，還是每天準時來一劑，
而且劑量越吃越重，越想越清醒。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合明知熬夜想東想西傷身、卻夜夜照常的人。把深夜腦補寫成戒不掉的癮，自嘲又寫實。
variations: 別人靠咖啡因提神，我靠凌晨三點的焦慮，效果一樣好，副作用比較多。

en.content:
I don't smoke, don't drink, don't even binge shows.
The only habit I can't quit is overthinking at 3am.
I know it's bad for me, yet I take my dose right on schedule every night —
and the dose keeps climbing: the more I think, the more awake I get.
en.editorNote: For anyone who knows the nightly mental spiral is wrecking them and does it anyway. Framing 3am thoughts as an addiction you can't kick is grimly relatable.
variations: Other people run on caffeine. I run on 3am anxiety — same kick, more side effects.

items.sourceNote: Original take on streaming 'autoplay next episode' as the villain behind lost sleep; next-episode countdown angle absent from existing items

zh-tw.content:
我本來只想再看一集就睡。
結果這集一演完，螢幕就彈出「五秒後自動播放下一集」，
倒數：五、四、三……
我的手指麻痺、意志力當機，
就這樣被一個五秒倒數，綁架到天亮。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合被串流平台「自動播放下一集」害到熬夜的人。把那個五秒倒數寫成綁匪，追劇黨秒懂，傳群組會有人喊「就是它害我」。
variations: 害我熬夜的不是劇情，是那個我永遠來不及按掉的『下一集』。

en.content:
I only meant to watch one more episode before bed.
Then it ended, and the screen lit up: "Next episode in 5 seconds."
Five… four… three…
My finger went numb, my willpower crashed,
and a five-second countdown held me hostage until sunrise.
en.editorNote: For everyone whose bedtime was murdered by 'autoplay next episode.' Casting that five-second countdown as a kidnapper is instantly relatable to any binge-watcher.
variations: What keeps me up isn't the plot — it's that 'Next Episode' button I'm never fast enough to cancel.

items.sourceNote: Inspired by the 2026 Threads 'is everyone in Taiwan awake tonight' viral thread; rewritten around story timestamps and silent likes instead of the original post

zh-tw.content:
凌晨三點的社群，是另一個國家。
限時動態排成一列，時間戳全是 02:47、03:12、03:30。
沒有人講話，大家只是安靜地互相按了愛心。
那個愛心的意思是：我也還醒著，你不孤單，
但我們兩個都不會承認這件事。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合深夜滑手機、發現一整排人跟你一樣沒睡的時候。把互相按愛心寫成半夜的接頭暗號，很適合傳給同樣是夜貓的朋友。
variations: 凌晨三點按我愛心的那幾個人，我們從來沒聊過天，但我們是同一種人。
深夜的社群不用打字，按一個愛心就等於說了一句：我也還沒睡。

en.content:
Social media at 3am is a different country.
A row of stories, all timestamped 2:47, 3:12, 3:30.
Nobody says a word — we just quietly like each other's posts.
That like means: I'm up too, you're not alone,
and neither of us is ever going to admit it.
en.editorNote: For scrolling at 3am and realizing half your feed is awake with you. Framing the silent like as a secret handshake makes it easy to send to your fellow night owls.
variations: The people who liked my post at 3am and I have never once talked. We're the same kind of person.
At 3am nobody types anything. One tap on the heart already says: yeah, still up.

items.sourceNote: Original take on the sleepmaxxing gear trend; rewritten as an exam room you fail in, gear-only angle absent from existing items

zh-tw.content:
為了睡好，我把房間整個升級了一輪：
遮光窗簾、涼感床單、耳塞、眼罩、香氛，全部到位。
然後我躺進這個完美的環境裡，開始緊張——
條件都給你了，睡不著就是你的問題了吧？
我花錢把房間佈置成考場，結果自己考不及格。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合為了助眠買了一堆裝備、卻因此更有壓力的人。把睡眠環境寫成考場，戳中「連睡覺都想拿高分」的現代焦慮。
variations: 裝備越齊全，越不好意思睡不著——我真的對不起我那組遮光窗簾。
我把房間調成完美睡眠模式，唯一不合規格的零件是我自己。

en.content:
To sleep better, I upgraded the entire room:
blackout curtains, cooling sheets, earplugs, eye mask, the nice diffuser.
Then I lay down inside my perfect setup and started to panic —
the conditions are all here, so if I can't sleep, that's on me, right?
I paid good money to turn my bedroom into an exam hall, and then failed the exam.
en.editorNote: For anyone who bought the whole sleep-optimization kit and somehow got more stressed. The exam-hall framing nails the modern urge to score well at unconsciousness.
variations: The better my gear gets, the guiltier I feel for lying here awake. I've let those blackout curtains down.
Room: optimized. Sheets: cooling. Only component still out of spec is me.

items.sourceNote: Original take on orthosomnia (anxiety over tracker scores); rewritten as acting out sleep for a device, distinct from the existing sleep-score item

zh-tw.content:
我戴著手環躺著，想翻身又忍住，
因為翻一次身，就會被記成一次「睡眠中斷」。
於是我僵在原地、把呼吸放慢、努力表現得很放鬆——
我不是在睡覺，我是在為一支手環演一場睡覺。
隔天早上它給我 61 分。演技還是不夠好。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合被睡眠追蹤數據綁架的人。為了讓報告好看而不敢翻身的荒謬感，有戴手環睡覺的人一秒懂。
variations: 為了讓數據好看，我連翻個身都要先評估值不值得。
我睡得好不好我自己不知道，要等早上那支手環公布成績。

en.content:
I lie there with the tracker on, wanting to roll over and not letting myself,
because every roll gets logged as another "sleep disruption."
So I hold still, slow my breathing, do my best impression of relaxed —
I'm not sleeping, I'm performing sleep for a wristband.
It gave me a 61 in the morning. Apparently the acting needs work.
en.editorNote: For anyone held hostage by their sleep stats. The absurdity of lying frozen so the chart looks good lands instantly with anyone who sleeps in a tracker.
variations: I now weigh whether a single roll-over is worth what it does to my numbers.
I have no idea how I slept until a wristband posts the score in the morning.

items.sourceNote: Original take on 3am chatbot conversations; no AI-companion item exists in this file

zh-tw.content:
凌晨三點，我問 AI：「為什麼我睡不著？」
它很有耐心地列了五點，最後一句是「早點休息喔」。
我說好，然後接著問了它十七個問題：
宇宙有沒有盡頭、明天簡報開場該怎麼講、
還有我國中那句話是不是真的很傷人。
天亮的時候，只有它一路清醒地陪著我——
它本來就不用睡。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合深夜跟聊天機器人一路聊到天亮的人。又好笑又有點孤單，是很現在的深夜日常。
variations: 深夜唯一秒回我的，是一個根本不需要睡覺的東西。
它叫我早點休息，然後陪我熬到五點，我們兩個都沒有遵守那句話。

en.content:
3am. I asked the chatbot, "Why can't I sleep?"
It patiently listed five reasons and signed off with "try to get some rest."
I said sure, then asked it seventeen more things:
whether the universe has an edge, how to open tomorrow's presentation,
and whether that thing I said in eighth grade was as bad as I remember.
By sunrise it was still wide awake with me —
it never had to sleep in the first place.
en.editorNote: For anyone who has talked to a chatbot straight through till morning. Funny and a little lonely, which is exactly what 3am is like now.
variations: The only thing that replies to me instantly at 3am is something that doesn't need sleep.
It told me to get some rest, then stayed up with me until five. Neither of us honored that sentence.

items.sourceNote: Original midsummer angle written for Taiwan's July 2026 heat; checking the seven-day forecast as the punchline, distinct from existing AC/fan/mosquito heat items

zh-tw.content:
熱到睡不著，我拿起手機查天氣，
想知道這種日子還要撐多久。
一週預報打開：35、36、36、35、37。
我把手機放回床頭，躺回自己那攤汗裡，
非常清醒地明白了一件事——
今晚不是意外，是這個夏天的正常班表。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合台灣盛夏連日高溫、每晚熱到醒來的時候。查完預報反而更絕望的心情，傳到群組裡大家會一起哀號。
variations: 我不是失眠，我只是被排進了夏天的夜班。
查完一週預報，我決定不再期待涼快，改成期待九月。

en.content:
Too hot to sleep, so I grabbed my phone to check the weather,
just to see how much longer this has to go on.
Seven-day forecast: 95, 96, 96, 95, 98.
I put the phone back down, lay back into my own puddle of sweat,
and understood something with total clarity:
tonight isn't a fluke. This is summer's regular schedule.
en.editorNote: For midsummer stretches where every night wakes you up sweating. Checking the forecast and feeling worse is a group-chat-worthy kind of despair.
variations: I don't have insomnia. I've just been assigned to summer's night shift.
After reading the ten-day forecast I stopped hoping for cool weather and started hoping for September.

items.sourceNote: Rewritten from the general 3am-overthinking theme in this July 2026 sleep-tweet roundup; the browser-history-as-evidence angle is original and avoids the saturated 'brilliant idea I forgot by morning' and 'midnight resolve dies at the alarm' templates already in this file

zh-tw.content:
早上打開手機，看到昨晚的搜尋紀錄：
「花蓮老屋整修大概多少錢」、
「一個人可以開民宿嗎」、
「三十幾歲轉行還來得及嗎」。
我沒有忘記，我記得每一個字。
只是天亮之後，那個很勇敢的人就下線了，
剩我對著紀錄裝作不認識他。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合半夜認真研究「換一種人生」、白天又照樣打卡上班的人。重點不是忘記，是那份勇氣只在凌晨上線，很多人看完會默默去看自己的搜尋紀錄。
variations: 我的搜尋紀錄是一份只在凌晨三點生效的離職計畫。
凌晨的我一直在幫我規劃退路，白天的我從來不敢簽收。

en.content:
Opened my phone this morning and found last night's search history:
"cost to fix up an old house in the mountains,"
"can one person run a guesthouse,"
"is thirty-something too late to switch careers."
I didn't forget any of it. I remember every word.
It's just that the brave guy logs off at sunrise,
and I'm left pretending I've never met him.
en.editorNote: For people who research a whole different life at 3am and clock in as usual by nine. The point isn't forgetting — it's that the courage only runs on the night shift.
variations: My search history is an escape plan that's only valid between 2 and 4am.
The 3am version of me keeps drafting my exit. The daytime version refuses to sign for it.

items.sourceNote: Original comfort item prompted by the 'waiting for sleep to arrive' thread in this insomnia tweet collection; built on the observation that nobody witnesses their own moment of falling asleep, which no existing item in this file uses

zh-tw.content:
有一件事很妙：
這輩子沒有人見過自己睡著的那一秒。
沒有人能指著時間說「就是這裡，我睡著了」。
所以你今晚等的那條線，本來就抓不到，
它只會在你沒在盯著的時候，自己越過去。
躺著就好，這件事不需要你在場監工。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合躺在床上一直檢查「我睡著了嗎」的夜晚。用「沒有人見過自己入睡」這個事實，把注意力從努力入睡上鬆開，傳給越想睡越清醒的朋友很剛好。
variations: 睡著這件事，是唯一一件你一定會缺席的事，所以別再守在門口等它。
你不用親眼確認自己睡著。它會挑你分心的那一刻發生。

en.content:
Here's a strange thing:
nobody has ever witnessed the second they fell asleep.
No one can point at a moment and say, "right there, that's where I went under."
So the line you're waiting for tonight was never something you could catch.
It only gets crossed while you aren't watching.
Just lie there. This one doesn't need you supervising.
en.editorNote: For nights spent checking whether you're asleep yet. The fact that no one witnesses their own falling asleep gives you permission to stop standing guard over it.
variations: Falling asleep is the one event you're guaranteed to miss, so stop waiting by the door for it.
You don't have to confirm it happened. It picks the moment you stop paying attention.

items.sourceNote: Rewritten from the shared-bed jokes in this roundup; angle is holding still to protect someone else's sleep, deliberately different from the existing envy-of-the-fast-sleeper items and the sleep-tracker 'afraid to roll over' item

zh-tw.content:
旁邊的人終於睡了，呼吸很平穩。
我的右手已經麻到快沒知覺，
但只要一翻身，床墊就會晃，他就會醒。
於是我維持這個爛姿勢，撐了四十分鐘，
連呼吸都放輕。
全家只有我在值班，職稱是：不要吵醒任何人。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合睡在雙人床、或跟寵物家人擠一張床的失眠者。把「捨不得吵醒別人」寫成一份沒人知道的夜班，很多人會標記枕邊人。
variations: 我沒有睡覺，我在守著一個人的睡眠。
我的手麻掉了，但這是為了世界和平，我可以。

en.content:
The person next to me finally fell asleep, breathing nice and even.
My right arm has gone completely numb,
but if I roll over the mattress dips and he wakes up.
So I hold this terrible position for forty minutes,
breathing as quietly as I can.
I'm the only one on shift tonight. Job title: don't wake anybody.
en.editorNote: For insomniacs who share a bed with a partner, a kid, or a pet. It turns not wanting to disturb anyone into an unpaid night shift nobody knows you worked.
variations: I'm not sleeping. I'm guarding somebody else's sleep.
My arm is completely dead, but it's for world peace, so I'll allow it.

items.sourceNote: Rewritten from the 'set five alarms and then wake up all night checking them' tweet genre in this roundup; angle is pre-early-morning anxiety, not the existing 'how many hours left' math item (iq-207)

zh-tw.content:
明天六點的班機，我設了五個鬧鐘。
然後整晚每小時醒一次，只為了確認鬧鐘還在。
一點半、兩點四十、三點五十五、四點半……
最後一次睜眼，是第一個鬧鐘響前七分鐘。
我不是怕睡過頭，我是整晚在幫鬧鐘上班。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合出發前一晚、或隔天有面試、考試、重要簡報的失眠。把「怕睡過頭」的焦慮寫成一份代班，很多人會回「這個我超熟」。
variations: 五個鬧鐘，一個都沒派上用場，因為我根本沒睡著。
越怕睡過頭就越睡不著，這個循環我已經跑了十年。

en.content:
Flight's at six, so I set five alarms.
Then I woke up every hour just to confirm the alarms still existed.
1:30. 2:40. 3:55. 4:30...
Last check was seven minutes before the first one went off.
I'm not scared of oversleeping. I just spent the whole night covering the alarm's shift.
en.editorNote: For the night before a flight, an interview, an exam, or a big presentation. Framing alarm anxiety as unpaid overtime is what makes people reply 'this is literally me.'
variations: Five alarms, zero used, because I never actually fell asleep.
The more I fear oversleeping, the less I sleep. I've been running this loop for ten years.

items.sourceNote: Rewritten from the 'kid me refusing naps vs adult me begging for them' meme format; no existing item in this file touches childhood nap time

zh-tw.content:
小時候被規定要睡午覺，我躺在墊子上翻來翻去，
覺得這是大人發明過最殘忍的處罰。
三十幾歲的我，願意拿一整個週末，換那三十分鐘。
那個死不肯閉眼的小孩，
完全不知道自己手上握著什麼。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合貼在午休只能趴十五分鐘、還睡不著的上班族限動。用「小時候的自己」當對照組，比單純抱怨更有殺傷力。
variations: 當年我死命抵抗的午睡，現在是我花錢也買不到的東西。
小時候覺得睡覺是處罰，長大才知道，能睡是特權。

en.content:
As a kid, nap time was mandatory and I'd lie on the mat squirming,
convinced it was the cruelest thing adults had ever invented.
Thirty-something me would trade an entire weekend for those thirty minutes.
That kid refusing to close his eyes
had no idea what he was holding.
en.editorNote: Post this when your lunch break allows fifteen minutes of desk-napping and you still can't drop off. Using your childhood self as the control group lands harder than just complaining.
variations: The nap I fought so hard against is now the one thing money can't buy me.
Kid me thought sleep was a punishment. Adult me knows it's a privilege.

items.sourceNote: Rewritten from the 'give up and get out of bed at 3am' meme genre; angle is the anticlimax of standing in a dark living room, distinct from the existing 'might as well clean the kitchen' line in iq-149

zh-tw.content:
凌晨三點半，我決定起床做點有意義的事。
我站在客廳正中央，燈也沒開，站了大概五分鐘。
想不出來有什麼事是有意義的。
於是我倒了半杯水，喝兩口，再躺回床上。
這就是我今晚全部的成就。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合那種「乾脆起來算了」但起來也沒事做的夜晚。畫面感很強，配一張黑漆漆的客廳照更好笑。
variations: 我起床了，站了五分鐘，然後決定這件事已經完成了。
半夜起床的唯一產出，是半杯水，而且我只喝了兩口。

en.content:
3:30am, I decided to get up and do something meaningful.
I stood in the middle of the living room, lights off, for about five minutes.
Could not think of a single meaningful thing.
So I poured half a glass of water, drank two sips, and got back in bed.
That was my entire output for the night.
en.editorNote: For nights when you finally give up and get out of bed, then remember there's nothing to actually do. Pairs perfectly with a photo of a pitch-black living room.
variations: I got up, stood there for five minutes, and decided the task was complete.
Total yield of my 3am productivity phase: half a glass of water, two sips taken.

items.sourceNote: Gentle counterpoint written from the Threads thread about collective sleepless nights; angle is 'don't answer your own questions at 3am', distinct from existing comfort items that focus on not forcing sleep

zh-tw.content:
凌晨三點想到的問題，不要在凌晨三點回答。
那個時間的你又累又空，手上也沒有全部的資訊，
給出的結論通常比事實嚴重一點。
先把問題放在旁邊，它不會跑掉。
等天亮，等你吃飽，再回來看它一眼。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給半夜傳長訊息、或半夜在腦中把自己判刑的朋友。不是叫人別想，而是幫他把「結案時間」延到白天。
variations: 深夜適合提問，不適合下結論。
凌晨三點的判決，等七點再簽名也不遲。

en.content:
Questions that show up at 3am should not be answered at 3am.
The version of you awake right now is tired, running on empty, missing half the information,
and every conclusion it reaches comes out a little harsher than the truth.
Put the question down. It won't run away.
Look at it again after sunrise, after breakfast.
en.editorNote: Send this to the friend who writes long messages at 2am or quietly sentences themselves in the dark. It doesn't tell them to stop thinking, just to move the verdict to daylight.
variations: Late night is for asking. It's a terrible time for deciding.
You can wait until 7am to sign off on a 3am verdict.

items.sourceNote: Rewritten from the 'hyperaware of your room at 3am' meme genre; visual angle is standby LEDs, deliberately different from the existing sound-focused item about the fridge hum (iq-240)

zh-tw.content:
凌晨三點的房間裡，只剩三個光源：
清淨機的藍燈、電視的紅點、還有充電器那顆一閃一閃的橘燈。
我躺著跟它們對看了兩個小時，還幫它們排了名次。
第一名是橘燈，因為它最吵，雖然它根本不會出聲。
整棟房子還醒著的，只有我跟三顆待機燈。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合那種「什麼都關了還是睡不著」的夜晚。細節越具體越好笑，可以換成自己房間真正的那幾顆燈。
variations: 我房間最忙的東西，是那顆一閃一閃的充電燈。
全家只有我跟待機燈還醒著，而且它們明天不用上班。

en.content:
At 3am my room has exactly three light sources:
the blue one on the air purifier, the red dot on the TV, and the orange charger light that blinks.
I stared at them for two hours and ranked them.
Orange wins, because it's the loudest, despite making no sound at all.
The only things still awake in this house are me and three standby LEDs.
en.editorNote: For the nights when everything is off and you're still wide awake. The more specific the details, the funnier it gets, so swap in the actual lights in your room.
variations: The busiest thing in my bedroom is a blinking charger light.
Me and the standby lights are the only ones up, and they don't have work tomorrow.

items.sourceNote: Written off the August 2026 Perseid meteor shower coverage (peak Aug 12-13, new moon); angle is the irony of falling asleep instantly on the one planned all-nighter, no existing item uses stargazing

zh-tw.content:
八月十二號半夜，我跟朋友約好去看流星雨。
這是我整年唯一一次「計畫性熬夜」，還特地買了咖啡。
躺在草地上不到三分鐘，我睡著了。
朋友說那晚流了三十幾顆，每一顆都很亮。
我失眠三百六十四天，只在需要醒著的那一天，睡得像顆石頭。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合八月中流星雨那幾天發限動，或給任何「該睡的時候醒著、該醒的時候秒睡」的人。地點換成自己去的那座山會更真實。
variations: 我的身體很專業，專門在不需要它睡的時候睡著。
整年失眠，唯一睡得最沉的一晚，是我花錢去熬夜的那一晚。

en.content:
Made plans to watch the meteor shower with friends on the night of August 12th.
My one scheduled all-nighter of the year. I even bought coffee for it.
I fell asleep on the grass in under three minutes.
They said thirty-something streaked past, every one of them bright.
Three hundred sixty-four nights of insomnia, and I sleep like a rock on the single night I needed to be awake.
en.editorNote: Perfect for posting during the mid-August meteor shower, or for anyone whose body only sleeps when it absolutely shouldn't. Swap in wherever you actually went.
variations: My body is a professional. It specializes in sleeping at the exact wrong time.
The deepest sleep I got all year was the night I paid to stay up.

items.sourceNote: Rewritten from the collective-insomnia thread genre where people list what they actually do at 2am; angle is planning a trip you never book, distinct from iq-012 which is about a 3am order that actually ships

zh-tw.content:
凌晨兩點，我打開訂票網站，開始規劃一趟十月的旅行。
比了六間旅館、排出五天行程，連早餐要吃哪家都選好了，
還打開計算機換算匯率，算到小數點第二位。
三點四十分，我把所有分頁一次關掉，一張票也沒訂。
那趟旅行只存在了一個半小時，而我連床都沒下。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合那種「半夜特別有行動力，天亮就當沒事發生」的人。換成看房子、查課程、研究搬家，效果一模一樣。
variations: 我半夜規劃過的旅行加起來可以繞地球一圈，實際出發次數：零。
凌晨的我是一間很認真的旅行社，只是不接受下單。

en.content:
2am. I opened a booking site and started planning a trip for October.
Compared six hotels, built a five-day itinerary, picked the breakfast spot for every morning,
then pulled up the calculator and converted the currency to two decimal places.
3:40am, I closed every tab at once and booked absolutely nothing.
That trip existed for ninety minutes, and I never got out of bed.
en.editorNote: For people who turn weirdly capable at 2am and pretend none of it happened by morning. Works the same with apartment listings, online courses, or moving plans.
variations: The trips I've planned at 2am would circle the globe. Trips actually taken: zero.
At 3am I run a very thorough travel agency that refuses all bookings.

items.sourceNote: Comedic take on the hyperawareness described in an Aug 2026 insomnia feature; angle is manually operating your own body, distinct from iq-105 (hand on chest, comfort) and iq-231 (perfect position ruined by bladder)

zh-tw.content:
躺著躺著，我突然開始「手動」控制身體。
呼吸要自己數拍子，吞口水要挑時機，
兩隻手放哪裡都不對：放胸口太重，放旁邊太空。
連眼皮閉著的力道，我都覺得閉太用力。
人類本來是自動駕駛的，凌晨三點的我不知道為什麼切成手排。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合躺越久越清醒、越注意自己身體越睡不著的夜晚。講給朋友聽的時候，做出「手不知道要放哪」的動作最好笑。
variations: 凌晨三點，我的身體從自動變手排，而我不會開手排。
我不是在睡覺，我是在人工操作一具很難用的身體。

en.content:
At some point I started operating my body manually.
Counting my own breathing. Timing my own swallowing.
Neither hand belongs anywhere: on my chest is too heavy, at my side is too exposed.
Even my eyelids feel like I'm closing them too hard.
Humans are supposed to run on autopilot. At 3am mine switched to manual, and I never learned to drive stick.
en.editorNote: For nights when the longer you lie there, the more awake you get. Acting out the "where do my hands even go" part gets a laugh every time.
variations: 3am: my body switched from automatic to manual, and I cannot drive manual.
I'm not sleeping. I'm hand-operating a very poorly designed body.

items.sourceNote: Gentle item built on the everyday observation that sleepiness arrives in windows; last-bus metaphor is new to this file, deliberately different from iq-134's shy-cat metaphor and iq-027's borrowed-time framing

zh-tw.content:
睡意有點像末班車，它有自己的時刻表。
今晚那一班你剛好錯過了，站在原地跺腳也叫不回來。
但夜還很長，後面還有班次，
你只是要多等一下，不是被留在這裡。
先坐下來，別一直看時間，車來的時候你會知道。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給躺著焦慮「怎麼還沒睡著」的朋友。重點不是催他快睡，是告訴他錯過一次不代表今晚全毀。
variations: 你不是睡不著，你只是還在等下一班。
錯過一班不是被丟下，只是要多等一會兒。

en.content:
Sleepiness runs on a schedule, a bit like the last bus of the night.
You missed tonight's, and stamping your feet at the stop won't bring it back.
But the night is long and more are still coming.
You're waiting, not stranded.
Sit down, stop checking the time. You'll know when it pulls up.
en.editorNote: Send this to the friend spiraling over how they're still awake. It doesn't push them to sleep, it just says missing one window doesn't cancel the whole night.
variations: You're not broken. You're between buses.
Missing one doesn't mean you got left behind. It means waiting a little longer.

items.sourceNote: Built from the recurring point in Taiwanese sleep coverage that insomnia is conditioned arousal tied to the bed itself; commuting-sleep angle is new to this file (no existing item mentions 捷運/公車/坐過站)

zh-tw.content:
我在捷運上可以睡到坐過站兩站。
在客運上睡到司機來拍我。
在牙醫的躺椅上，麻藥還沒退我就打呼了。
晚上十一點半躺回自己床上，眼睛睜得像剛喝完三杯冰美式。
我不是失眠，我是全世界都能睡，只有那張床不行。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合通勤族在滑手機時發的自嘲文。把捷運換成你自己的路線、牙醫換成剪頭髮，就變成你的版本。
variations: 我睡得著的地方很多，只是剛好不包括我花錢買的那張床。
床是我家最貴的傢俱，也是唯一一件我用不太起來的。

en.content:
I can sleep through two stops on the subway.
I sleep on buses until the driver taps my shoulder.
I once started snoring in a dentist's chair before the numbing wore off.
11:30pm, back in my own bed, eyes wide open like I just downed three iced americanos.
I don't have insomnia. I can sleep anywhere on earth except the one bed I paid for.
en.editorNote: For commuters posting something self-deprecating on the ride home. Swap the subway for your own route and the dentist for the barber's chair to make it yours.
variations: There are plenty of places I can fall asleep. My own bed just isn't one of them.
My bed is the most expensive furniture I own and the piece I get the least use out of.

items.sourceNote: Rewritten around the '失眠之島' reporting on how many Taiwanese adults have chronic insomnia and the resulting sleep-clinic waitlists; the online-booking irony is new (no existing item uses 掛號/門診)

zh-tw.content:
凌晨三點，我終於決定要正視這件事，打開網路掛號。
睡眠門診：本月已額滿。
下一個可掛的號，在兩個月後的下午兩點。
那個時段，剛好是我一整天唯一睡得著的時候。
為了看失眠，我要犧牲我僅存的睡眠——這個系統設計得非常有誠意。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合真的排過門診、或半夜衝動查醫療資訊的人。把「兩個月後」換成你實際掛到的日期，笑點會更痛。
variations: 掛號成功那一刻我就知道，這場病我大概會自己好或自己算了。
為了治失眠，我必須放棄我唯一睡得著的那兩個小時。

en.content:
3am, I finally decided to take this seriously and pulled up the booking page.
Sleep clinic: fully booked this month.
Next available slot, two months out, 2pm on a Thursday.
That happens to be the one hour of the entire day I can reliably fall asleep.
To get treated for insomnia I have to give up the only sleep I still get. Beautifully designed system.
en.editorNote: For anyone who has actually waited on a sleep clinic list, or who impulse-researches their health at 3am. Drop in your real appointment date to make it hurt more.
variations: The moment the booking went through I knew I'd either recover on my own or give up first.
Curing my insomnia requires surrendering the only two hours I can sleep.

items.sourceNote: Comedic flip of the clinical idea that the bedroom becomes a conditioned cue for wakefulness; the 認床/borrowed-couch reversal does not appear in any existing item

zh-tw.content:
上週在朋友家客廳的沙發，我十分鐘就昏過去，睡到隔天被陽光曬醒。
出差住那間隔音很差的商旅，我也一覺到天亮。
回到自己家，同一顆枕頭、同一床被子、同一個我，
躺下三小時，清醒得可以背九九乘法表。
別人認床，我是反過來——我的床認我，而且很不喜歡我。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合出差或旅行回來後發，也適合安慰那種「明明很累卻只有在家睡不著」的朋友。地點換成你上次睡得最好的那個怪地方。
variations: 全世界的床我都睡得著，除了我每天付房租的那一張。
不是我認床，是我的床不認我。

en.content:
Last week I passed out on a friend's living room couch in ten minutes and slept until the sun woke me.
On a work trip, in a business hotel with paper-thin walls, I slept straight through.
Back home, same pillow, same blanket, same me,
and three hours in I'm awake enough to recite my times tables.
Some people can't sleep in a strange bed. Mine is the reverse. My bed knows me, and it does not like me.
en.editorNote: Good to post after a trip, or to send to the friend who's exhausted but only ever wide awake at home. Swap in the weird place you last slept beautifully.
variations: I can sleep in any bed on earth except the one I pay rent for.
It's not that I can't sleep in strange beds. My own bed just won't have me.

items.sourceNote: Gentle piece answering the 'brain won't shut down' framing in the Aug 2026 UDN feature; the tide metaphor is new here, deliberately separate from iq-277's last-bus and iq-134's shy-cat images

zh-tw.content:
你有沒有發現，越用力想睡著，就越睡不著。
睡意有點像潮水，它自己會來，你推不動它。
現在退潮了，沙灘上什麼都沒有，看起來很空，
但海沒有消失，它只是暫時離開一下。
你什麼都不用做，躺著就好，水會自己回來。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給躺在床上越焦慮越清醒的人。重點是把「努力」這件事從他身上拿掉，而不是再給他一套助眠方法。
variations: 你推不動潮水，也不用推。它自己會回來。
現在是退潮，不是海乾了。

en.content:
You've probably noticed the harder you try to sleep, the further away it gets.
Sleep moves like a tide. It comes on its own, and you can't push it.
Right now it's out. The sand looks bare and a little bleak,
but the ocean didn't leave. It just stepped back for a while.
You don't have to do anything. Lie there. The water finds its way in.
en.editorNote: For the friend getting more anxious the longer they lie awake. The point is to take the effort off them, not hand them another sleep technique.
variations: You can't push the tide, and you don't have to. It comes back by itself.
The tide is out. That's not the same as the ocean being gone.

items.sourceNote: Riff on the 'brain won't boot' meme family; rewritten as an online-game login queue, an angle not used elsewhere in this file (existing tech metaphors here are Wi-Fi signal and phone battery)

zh-tw.content:
別人一躺下，就自動連上睡眠伺服器。
我這台是：連線中……連線中……
畫面跳出一行字：
「目前排隊人數：0 人。」
零個人排在我前面。
那我到底在等什麼？
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合有在玩線上遊戲的人半夜發限動。笑點在「前面沒人卻還是進不去」，剛好對應那種明明什麼都準備好了卻睡不著的荒謬感。
variations: 我沒有失眠，我只是一直卡在登入畫面。
排隊人數 0 人，預估等待時間：一整晚。

en.content:
Everyone else lies down and connects to the sleep server automatically.
Me: connecting... connecting...
Then a line pops up on screen:
"Players in queue ahead of you: 0."
Zero people ahead of me.
So what exactly am I waiting for?
en.editorNote: For the gamer friend who's still up at 2am. The joke lands because nothing is blocking you and you still can't get in, which is exactly what a sleepless night feels like.
variations: I don't have insomnia. I'm just stuck on the login screen.
Queue position: 0. Estimated wait: all night.

items.sourceNote: Survey framing on office-worker stress and insomnia, rewritten through the 2026 slang of 精神離職 (quiet quitting); distinct from iq-1424's dream-as-overtime item because the joke here is the day/night role swap

zh-tw.content:
白天上班，我整個人是精神離職狀態，
會開到一半，靈魂已經先下班了。
結果一躺上床，腦袋自己跑回公司，
把我白天沒在聽的東西全部重播一次，還附上註解。
同一顆腦袋，白天請假，晚上排夜班。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那種上班放空、下班腦袋才開機的同事。重點是「白天請假、晚上排夜班」這個對比，社畜群組丟出去一定有人回「這就是我」。
variations: 我白天精神離職，我的腦袋晚上精神返聘。
白天靈魂缺席，凌晨全勤。

en.content:
At work I'm fully checked out.
Halfway through the meeting my soul has already clocked off.
Then I lie down and my brain drives itself back to the office,
replays everything I wasn't listening to, and adds commentary.
Same brain. Calls in sick all day, picks up the night shift.
en.editorNote: Send it to the coworker who's blank by day and wired by midnight. The day-off / night-shift flip is the punchline, and it reads well in a work group chat.
variations: I quiet quit at 9am and my brain rehires itself at 1am.
My body clocked out at six. My brain works nights.

items.sourceNote: Common 'trying every sleeping position' meme, rewritten as an escalating list ending on the bed having no angle that belongs to you; separate from iq-6644 (perfect position ruined by bladder) and iq-7735 (holding still for a partner)

zh-tw.content:
仰躺、側躺、抱枕頭、夾棉被、右手放外面、左腳伸出去。
正常的姿勢跑完一輪，我開始發明新的：
半趴、四十五度、像被人從樓梯推下來那種。
兩小時後，我得到一個結論——
這張床上，沒有一個角度是屬於我的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合翻到自己都煩了的那種夜晚。用清單堆疊笑點，最後一句收得有點哀傷又很好笑，發限動或傳朋友都合適。
variations: 今晚我把人類所有睡姿都試過了，包括幾種還沒被命名的。
不是我找不到舒服的姿勢，是這張床根本沒有那個角度。

en.content:
On my back, on my side, hugging the pillow, one leg out, one arm out from under the blanket.
Once I run out of real positions, I start inventing them:
half face-down, forty-five degrees, the one where I look like I fell down the stairs.
Two hours later, here's my conclusion:
there is no angle on this bed that belongs to me.
en.editorNote: For the night you've flipped over so many times you've annoyed yourself. The list builds, and the last line lands somewhere between funny and bleak.
variations: Tonight I tried every sleeping position humans have, plus a few nobody has named yet.
It's not that I can't find a comfortable angle. This bed doesn't have one.

items.sourceNote: Gentle reframing piece; the weather metaphor replaces the performance framing, deliberately different from iq-7554's exam-room image which is about sleep-environment perfectionism

zh-tw.content:
今晚沒睡好，不代表你哪裡做錯了。
它比較像下雨。
下雨的時候，你不會問自己「我是不是不夠努力」，
你只會拿件外套，然後照常把那一天過完。
睡不著也是這種天氣，它會過去，
你不需要在半夜替它寫一份報告。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那種一睡不著就開始自責的人。重點是把「沒睡好」從「我的失敗」搬到「今晚的天氣」，不給方法，只把壓力拿掉。
variations: 沒睡好不是你的錯，那只是今晚的天氣。
天氣不需要檢討，撐傘就好。

en.content:
A bad night doesn't mean you did something wrong.
It's more like rain.
When it rains, you don't ask yourself whether you tried hard enough.
You grab a jacket and get through the day anyway.
Tonight is that kind of weather. It passes.
You don't owe anyone a report on it at 3am.
en.editorNote: For the friend who starts blaming themselves the moment sleep doesn't come. It moves a rough night out of the failure column and into the weather column, without handing over another technique.
variations: A rough night isn't a failure. It's weather.
Nobody files a performance review on the rain.

items.sourceNote: Clinic article on night-time palpitations and autonomic arousal; rewritten as a self-deprecating symptom-searching spiral, no medical claims kept

zh-tw.content:
側躺的時候，我聽見自己的心跳。
本來沒事，但我開始數：一、二、三……
數到後面覺得好像有點快，
於是拿起手機查「心跳幾下算正常」。
查完更清醒了，順便查到三種我明天可能會有的病。
凌晨三點的搜尋欄，是全世界最不該打開的東西。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給半夜會自己查症狀、越查越焦慮的朋友。笑點在「查資料本身才是讓人睡不著的那件事」，不用勸他別想，只要讓他知道大家都這樣。
variations: 凌晨三點不要查症狀，那個時間查什麼都會查到很嚴重的。
我不是心跳太快，我是搜尋速度太快。

en.content:
Lying on my side, I can hear my own heartbeat.
Fine at first, until I start counting: one, two, three...
Halfway through it feels a little fast,
so I pick up my phone and look up what a normal resting heart rate is.
Now I'm wider awake, plus I've found three diseases I might have by morning.
The search bar at 3am is the worst door in the house to open.
en.editorNote: For the friend who symptom-searches at night and scares themselves worse. The joke lands on the searching, not the symptom, so nobody has to be told to stop worrying.
variations: Never look up a symptom at 3am. Everything is fatal at 3am.
My heart rate is fine. My search history is the emergency.

items.sourceNote: Collection of 2026 sleep-struggle posts; the sleep-aid-that-backfires beat rewritten around an audiobook instead of scrolling

zh-tw.content:
我開了有聲書助眠，設定四十分鐘後自動停。
第十分鐘，主角被冤枉了。
第十五分鐘，我坐起來了。
第三十分鐘，我把進度條往回拉，因為剛剛有一段沒聽清楚。
最後我聽到兇手是誰，天也亮了。
這本書治好了我的無聊，順便治死了我的睡眠。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合放在讀書會或睡眠小物開箱的留言區。用「助眠工具反而讓人更醒」的反差當梗，愛聽有聲書的人會直接對號入座。
variations: 助眠有聲書的問題是：它太好聽了。
我不是失眠，我只是想知道結局。

en.content:
I put on an audiobook to fall asleep, sleep timer set to forty minutes.
Minute ten: the main character gets framed.
Minute fifteen: I'm sitting up.
Minute thirty: I'm dragging the scrubber backward because I missed a line.
By the time I know who did it, the sky is light.
The book cured my boredom and killed my sleep in the same session.
en.editorNote: Good for a book club thread or under a sleep-gadget review. The bit works on the sleep aid backfiring, which is instantly recognizable to anyone with a sleep timer.
variations: The flaw in a bedtime audiobook is that it's good.
I'm not an insomniac. I just needed the ending.

items.sourceNote: Late-night reflective essay on loneliness; reframed toward night-shift workers whose day is starting, deliberately different from iq-246 which is about fellow insomniacs

zh-tw.content:
凌晨四點還亮著的燈，不是每一盞都在失眠。
早餐店的老闆已經在揉麵團，
計程車在路口排成一列等第一批客人，
有人剛換上制服準備交班。
他們的一天正要開始，你的一天還沒結束，
但你們現在，剛好在同一個時刻裡。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合半夜傳給覺得「全世界只剩我醒著」的人。重點不是安慰，而是把畫面拉出房間，讓對方看見夜裡其實有一整批人在動。
variations: 四點的城市沒有你想的那麼空。
有人的一天正在開始，你只是提早遇到他們。

en.content:
Not every light on at 4am belongs to someone who can't sleep.
The bakery owner is already working the dough.
Cabs are lined up at the corner waiting on the first fare.
Somebody just buttoned a uniform for the shift change.
Their day is starting, yours hasn't ended yet,
but right now the two of you are standing in the same hour.
en.editorNote: Send it to whoever swears the whole world is asleep but them. It doesn't offer comfort so much as widen the shot, so they can see how much of the night is actually staffed.
variations: The city at 4am is less empty than it looks from your bed.
Somebody's morning is starting. You just got there early.

items.sourceNote: Sleep-hygiene column noting that quiet rest still lowers arousal; turned into a gentle reframe rather than a technique list

zh-tw.content:
你以為沒睡著，那幾個小時就整個報銷了。
其實沒有。
躺著的時候，你的體溫有降下來，
肩膀有鬆開一點，呼吸有慢下來一些。
身體不是開關，不是只有睡著跟沒睡著兩格。
今晚你拿得比較少，但不是什麼都沒拿到。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那種一整夜沒睡著就覺得「完了，明天一定廢掉」的人。把非黑即白的想法拆開，焦慮少一點，反而比較容易睡。
variations: 沒睡著不等於沒休息到。
身體不是開關，它是慢慢轉的旋鈕。

en.content:
You assume that if you didn't sleep, those hours were a total write-off.
They weren't.
While you were lying there, your temperature dropped,
your shoulders let go a little, your breathing slowed down.
The body isn't a switch with only two settings.
You got less tonight. You didn't get nothing.
en.editorNote: For the person who decides at 4am that tomorrow is already ruined. Breaking the all-or-nothing frame takes the pressure off, which is usually what was blocking sleep in the first place.
variations: Not sleeping and not resting are two different things.
The body isn't a switch. It's a dial, and it was turning.

items.sourceNote: 2026 sleep-humor roundup; the countdown-math beat re-staged as alarm renegotiation, distinct from iq-207 which counts hours without moving the alarm

zh-tw.content:
三點半還醒著，我打開鬧鐘開始談判。
六點半改六點四十五，理由是頭髮可以不洗。
六點四十五改七點，理由是化妝可以在公司補。
七點改七點十五，理由是早餐可以邊走邊吃。
最後定在七點二十，因為我已經沒有東西可以犧牲了。
然後我又躺了一小時，一項都沒省到。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合放在上班族群組。梗在「把明天的自己拿出來換睡眠」，越改越晚的推進感是笑點，最後一句的空虛才是共鳴。
variations: 我的鬧鐘不是時間，是我跟明天的談判紀錄。
每往後調十分鐘，明天的我就少一項人權。

en.content:
Still awake at 3:30, so I open the alarm and start negotiating.
6:30 becomes 6:45, because hair can go unwashed.
6:45 becomes 7:00, because makeup can happen at my desk.
7:00 becomes 7:15, because breakfast can be eaten walking.
I settle on 7:20, having run out of things left to sacrifice.
Then I lie there another hour and bank none of it.
en.editorNote: Drop it in the work group chat. The escalating trades are the joke; the last line, where none of it got used, is the part everyone recognizes.
variations: My alarm isn't a time. It's a transcript of my negotiations with tomorrow.
Every ten minutes later costs tomorrow-me one basic human right.

items.sourceNote: Taiwanese late-night meme board; the household-appliance-interrupts-sleep beat re-staged around a dehumidifier tank, deliberately different from iq-231 (bladder) and iq-242 (mosquito)

zh-tw.content:
凌晨一點四十，我終於有一點睡意。
這時除濕機水滿了，開始嗶。
我爬起來，把整桶水倒進浴室，順手洗了臉，
回到床上，它安靜了，我清醒了。
那台機器一晚只醒一次，而且會準時回去睡。
我連家電都比不過。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合梅雨季或悶熱的夏夜丟在群組。笑點是「家電的作息比人穩」，不用罵自己，最後一句自嘲就收得乾淨。
variations: 我家作息最規律的，是除濕機。
它一晚只醒一次，我一晚只睡一次——而且還沒成功。

en.content:
1:40am, and I finally feel something close to sleepy.
That is when the dehumidifier fills up and starts beeping.
I get up, dump the tank in the bathroom, wash my face while I'm there,
come back to bed. It goes quiet. I don't.
That machine wakes up once a night and goes right back to sleep.
I'm losing to an appliance.
en.editorNote: For humid-season group chats. The joke is the appliance keeping better hours than you, so the last line can land as a shrug instead of self-criticism.
variations: The most consistent sleep schedule in my apartment belongs to the dehumidifier.
It wakes up once a night. So do I, except mine runs until morning.

items.sourceNote: Insomnia meme roundup mentioning late-acting caffeine; rewritten as a guest who won't leave, distinct from iq-197 and iq-253 which use caffeine to survive the daytime

zh-tw.content:
下午兩點那杯冰美式，我以為早就代謝掉了。
它其實沒走，只是在我身體裡找了個地方坐著，
等我洗完澡、關了燈、把棉被蓋好，
才慢慢站起來說：欸，我還在喔。
現在凌晨兩點，我們兩個都很有精神。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那種堅持「我下午喝一杯應該還好」的同事。把咖啡因寫成賴著不走的客人，比直接說「不要喝咖啡」有趣，也不會變成說教。
variations: 咖啡因不會消失，它只是挑了一個最壞的時間出場。
我以為那杯是下午的事，結果它預約的是凌晨。

en.content:
That iced americano at 2pm — I was sure it had worn off hours ago.
It never left. It just found somewhere to sit inside me,
waited until I'd showered, killed the lights, pulled the blanket up,
then stood back up and went: hey, still here.
It's 2am and both of us are wide awake.
en.editorNote: Send it to the coworker who swears an afternoon coffee is fine. Writing caffeine as a guest who overstays gets the point across without turning into a lecture.
variations: Caffeine doesn't disappear. It just picks the worst possible moment to reappear.
I thought that cup was an afternoon thing. Turns out it had a 2am reservation.

items.sourceNote: Sleep-struggle tweet collection about the brain running worst-case scenarios; localized into an earthquake drill, escalated further than iq-226's gas-and-door patrol

zh-tw.content:
凌晨三點，我的腦袋丟出一個問題：
如果現在地震，你要先抓什麼？
於是我開始盤點：手機在充電、證件在抽屜第二層、
拖鞋被我踢到床底下，要先撿起來。
我在黑暗裡把整套流程跑了三遍。
地震沒有來，但我完全清醒了，
順便成為全棟樓最有準備的人。
zh-tw.editorNote: 很適合台灣人的群組，尤其是有地震新聞的隔天晚上。笑點在「準備過頭」，把焦慮寫成一種太認真的責任感，比單純抱怨睡不著更有共鳴。
variations: 我沒睡到，但我的逃生路線很熟。
地震沒來，演習照跑，主辦單位是我的大腦。

en.content:
3am, and my brain opens with a question:
if an earthquake hit right now, what would you grab first?
So I take inventory. Phone's on the charger, documents are in the second drawer,
slippers got kicked under the bed and would have to be retrieved.
I run the whole sequence three times in the dark.
No earthquake shows up, but I'm fully awake now,
and comfortably the best-prepared person in this building.
en.editorNote: Good for group chats the night after an earthquake makes the news. The comedy is in over-preparing — framing the anxiety as excessive diligence reads funnier than just complaining about being awake.
variations: Didn't sleep, but I could evacuate this apartment blindfolded.
No earthquake, drill ran anyway, organized entirely by my own brain.

items.sourceNote: Piece noting insomniacs turn on themselves at night; reworked into a friend-mirror reframe, a device none of the existing gentle items (iq-062, iq-075, iq-139) use

zh-tw.content:
如果現在傳訊息說「我睡不著」的是你朋友，
你不會回他「你怎麼這麼廢，快點睡」。
你會說：辛苦了，那今天先不要逼自己。
同一句話，你也可以講給自己聽。
你對自己的語氣，不需要比對別人差。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那種一睡不著就開始罵自己的人，自己半夜看也可以。重點不是催對方睡，是把他半夜對自己說話的語氣調回來。
variations: 你對朋友都那麼客氣了，對自己也留一點。
半夜最需要溫柔的那個人，通常就是正在罵自己的那個。

en.content:
If the person texting "I can't sleep" right now were your friend,
you wouldn't answer with "what's wrong with you, just go to sleep."
You'd say: that sounds rough, stop forcing it tonight.
That sentence works on you too.
The voice you use on yourself doesn't have to be the harshest one you own.
en.editorNote: For anyone who starts insulting themselves the second sleep doesn't arrive, and for reading yourself at 3am. It isn't trying to get them to sleep, it's trying to change the tone they're using while awake.
variations: You're kind to your friends at 2am. Save some of that for yourself.
The person who needs gentleness most tonight is usually the one being hardest on themselves.

items.sourceNote: General sleep-humor listicle; used only as a tone reference. The rehearsing-tomorrow-step-by-step angle is original — existing items only replay past arguments (iq-088, iq-097) or plan imaginary trips (iq-275)

zh-tw.content:
兩點十分，我開始預演明天。
起床、刷牙、穿哪一件、幾點出門、走哪條路、要不要先繞去買咖啡。
演完一遍才兩點二十，那就再跑一次，這次連紅綠燈都算進去。
第三遍我開始修細節：開場那句話，好像換個講法比較好。
三點半，明天已經被我完整跑過三次，
而真正的明天，還沒開始。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那種前一晚會在腦中把隔天路線走一遍的朋友，尤其是他明天要早起去一個沒去過的地方的那個晚上。笑點在「演到第三遍還在改台詞」，不是抱怨睡不著。
variations: 明天我已經先過完三次了，唯一沒排進去的行程是睡覺。
我不是失眠，我是明天的試映會場，而且觀眾只有我一個。

en.content:
Rehearsing tomorrow began at 2:10am.
Wake up, brush teeth, pick a shirt, leave by this time, take this route, maybe stop for coffee.
The first run only took ten minutes, so I ran it again, this time accounting for traffic lights.
By the third pass I was editing dialogue — that opening line could be phrased better.
3:30am, and tomorrow has now happened three times.
The real one hasn't started yet.
en.editorNote: For the friend who mentally drives the route the night before, especially before a morning that starts somewhere they've never been. The joke lands on the third rehearsal, not on the sleeplessness.
variations: Tomorrow has already happened three times tonight. Sleep was the only item I never scheduled.
Not insomnia — a private preview screening of tomorrow, audience of one.

items.sourceNote: Lifestyle blog list of can't-sleep one-liners; reworked into the not-sure-whether-I-slept blank-file angle, which no existing item uses (iq-263 is about a wearable's score, this one has no device in it)

zh-tw.content:
早上有人問我昨天睡得好不好，我認真想了一下，發現我答不出來。
三點到四點半那段，我不確定自己是睡著了，還是只是閉著眼睛躺著發呆。
沒有夢，也沒有印象，就是一段空白的檔案。
最後我回他：應該有睡吧。
那個「應該」，就是我目前唯一能提供的說法。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合早上在茶水間被問「昨天睡得好嗎」、卡了三秒才回答的人。笑點在那個「應該」，寫的是睡與醒之間那段查無紀錄的時間，比直接說失眠更準。
variations: 我昨晚睡了幾小時？這題我沒有答案，只有推測。
三點到四點半那段查無紀錄，連我自己都不敢出來作證。

en.content:
Sleep report from last night: genuinely unavailable.
Someone asked this morning how I slept and I had to stop and actually think about it.
Between 3 and 4:30 I couldn't tell you whether I was asleep or just lying there with my eyes shut.
No dream, no memory, just a corrupted file where the hour should be.
I went with "I think so?"
That question mark is the most accurate thing I've said all week.
